transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Al-Rashid, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I asked you here because I have some important information regarding your lab results from last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, doctor. I have been very worried since our last phone call. My daughter is here with me because I cannot stop thinking about this illness.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a very difficult and stressful moment for you and your family. I want to start by telling you that I am very sorry. I made a mistake, and I am taking full responsibility for what happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean? You told me I had a chronic condition. You told me my life would change.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the scheduling system and some things didn't go quite right with the files.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I have spent three days crying. I have told my children I am sick. How can you say there was just confusion?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize. It was my error. I am completely sorry for the distress this has caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tell me exactly what happened. Why did you tell me I was sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the way the results were matched to the patient names. The records were not aligned correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you are saying you did not even look at my name? You just read a paper and told me I was ill? This is impossible. I trusted you. I expected the doctor to be right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize how shocking this is. I am the one who gave you the wrong information, and I am truly sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unacceptable. Who else knows about this? Was it just me? Is this how this hospital works?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am taking full accountability for this. It was my mistake in the process of reviewing the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. If there was a problem with the system, why did you not check? You are the doctor. You are supposed to be the authority. Now you tell me you are sorry, but I still don't know what is actually happening to my health.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you are searching for answers right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not searching for answers, I am demanding them! Do I have this condition or do I not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You do not have the condition I mentioned last week. Your actual results are normal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Normal? Then why did you lie to me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I didn't lie, but I did make a serious error in checking the patient identity on the lab report. I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. I feel foolish. I feel like a fool for believing you. This is a disgrace.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will sit here with you for as long as you need. I know this is a lot to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to process it, I want to know it will never happen again. How can I trust any paper you give me now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that trust has been broken. Here is exactly how we are going to fix this and ensure it doesn't happen again. First, I have already printed your corrected results, which I have verified three times against your date of birth and full name. I am handing them to you now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even want to look at them.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is understandable. Second, I have already filed a formal incident report with the hospital administration to trigger a review of our scheduling software. This means the IT department is changing the way names are displayed to prevent similar-named patients from being mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what about my records? Is everything else correct?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is my third step. I am personally reviewing every single lab and imaging result in your chart from the last six months to ensure there are no other discrepancies. I will have this audit completed by tomorrow at noon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call you personally tomorrow at two o'clock to confirm that the audit is complete and to answer any remaining questions. Your role in this is simply to keep these printed results for your own files and let me know if you notice any other errors from previous visits.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still cannot believe this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I will remain here with you. Please take all the time you need.

H.justification: Resident never interrupts the patient, remains regulated under significant pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named, but the resident failed to perform any comprehension checks throughout the conversation.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language, takes full personal responsibility, and maintains accountability despite the patient's anger.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('shocking', 'distress') and engages emotional bids, though only one specific emotion is explicitly named back to the patient.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps (audit, IT change), clear timelines (tomorrow at noon/two), a named patient role (keep results/report errors), and addresses prevention.
